title: Source Member Ranges And Structural Relations Contract
summary: Bounded source declaration ranges, content identities, and fail-closed structural relations used by change-aware rereads.

release.compatibility: Shin v1.25 requires an explicit generator-v17 rebuild for corrected authority semantics. No compatibility reader or implicit migration is retained.

ownership.core: Owns bounded syntax observation, lexical fallback, raw-line span identity, relation candidate validation, deterministic sorting/deduplication, and generated links.jsonl parsing.
ownership.profiles: Own source roots, allowed source extensions, extractor selection, and source inventory. A profile does not change the parser's language grammar or relation resolution rules.
ownership.agents: Own interpretation of bounded evidence and whether a review is sufficient. Agents must not upgrade source observations into compiler, runtime, or execution proof.

nativeCppDevelopment.grammar: tree-sitter-cpp v0.23.4, f41e1a044c8a84ea9fa8577fdd2eab92ec96de02, MIT, vendored C11 with one explicit-void scanner prototype patch
nativeCppDevelopment.scope: Existing C++-classified extensions except .c. Observes named function declarations/definitions, constructors, destructors, operators and class/struct/enum/namespace definitions. Forward type references without bodies, anonymous/lambda names and unsupported declarators are not promoted into named definitions. No preprocessing, type checking, compile database or call resolution.
nativeCppDevelopment.identity: C++ syntax fact IDs append the observed name byte offset, retaining distinct same-line overloads. Physical-line ranges and their existing hashes may contain neighboring declarations. Readable headers preserve source signatures; short ASCII syntactic qualified names may supplement existing identifier terms without a new row schema.
nativeCppDevelopment.bounds: The common parser byte/node/progress caps remain. Declarator/owner traversal is bounded64 levels; observed name/header and qualification remain source data, not compiler identity. Valid nodes can survive an incomplete tree; capped/cancelled parsing without declarations retains explicitly lexical fallback. Conditional definitions are observations of source, not active build branches.
nativeCppDevelopment.compatibility: Explicit development rebuild is required. Old generator-v20 snapshots and frozen semantic controls remain owned by their pinned dev18 or Stable binary. No implicit reader, vector rebinding or consumer delivery.

treeSitter.vendorBoundary: The grammars and runtime are vendored under third_party and built into the syntax library. Tree-sitter Unicode data carries the ICU/Unicode data license and notices in third_party/tree-sitter/src/unicode/LICENSE.

extensions.unsupportedBySyntaxParser: Other extensions, including .c, use their existing source-fact path or remain outside this syntax contract. Objective-C-family header selection is specified above.

validDeclarations.validity: A declaration is emitted only when its recognized Tree-sitter node has a safe name, a valid byte range, and no node error. TypeScript method definitions, method signatures, and abstract method signatures map to method; variable declarators map to arrow-function only when their value is an arrow_function.
validDeclarations.decorators: For TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, and JSX, a contiguous preceding decorator chain extends the declaration start line. Java declaration ranges start at the recognized declaration node.
validDeclarations.javaTopLevel: top_level is true only when a Java declaration node is directly under program. It controls qualified-type relation bindings; it does not mean that all emitted Java methods or constructors are top-level.
validDeclarations.malformedOrCapped: complete=false means parsing or bounded cursor traversal did not observe a complete tree. Valid observed declarations may still be emitted, plus a syntax-incomplete fact; completeness is not inferred from an absence of error nodes alone.
validDeclarations.overcapOrCancelledWithoutErrors: When traversal is over cap or cancelled without error nodes and no declarations were observed, existing TypeScript/JavaScript legacy header facts retain range_origin=lexical and syntax-incomplete is emitted; no fake precise syntax range is created.
validDeclarations.actualSyntaxErrors: When malformed syntax produces error nodes, valid declarations from the observed error-free CST portions are preserved only, while invalid nodes are not emitted as precise declarations.

headersAndImports.javaPackage: The first valid package declaration yields a package fact and package_line.
headersAndImports.javaImports: Only explicit Java imports are observed. Static and wildcard imports are excluded from this exact relation path.
headersAndImports.relativeModuleSyntax: TypeScript/JavaScript/TSX/JSX syntax relations accept only plain quoted relative literals beginning with ./ or ../, without escapes or embedded line breaks, from import_statement or export_statement nodes.
headersAndImports.externalModules: Non-relative module specifiers are not resolved by this bounded source relation adapter and are skipped without a relation row.
headersAndImports.unsupportedImportSyntax: Imports that are not recognized plain quoted relative literals are skipped entirely. A recognized relative literal with no indexed candidate is unresolved; unsupported syntax is not converted into an unresolved row.

fallback.guarantee: These languages do not receive Tree-sitter exact declaration ranges from this contract. Their lexical ranges remain source observations and can be incomplete or broader than a compiler declaration. The development-only C++ extension is owned by nativeCppDevelopment; older release baselines remain historical.

nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.grammar: tree-sitter-objcpp 0.1.0, pinned f744aa49e05971a2177f9b993f81a494744df7f5; MIT; vendored C11, ABI15. No Cocoa SDK or Objective-C compiler dependency.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.scope: Objective-C .m and mixed Objective-C++ .mm. Observes interfaces, implementations, protocols, categories, extensions, properties, complete method selectors, and ordinary C++ declarations. Message sends are not definitions. Quoted literal local #import/#include targets remain candidates subject to existing project-owned relation validation; system and macro imports are not resolved.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.headers: Valid C++ .h/.hh/.hpp/.hxx retain the C++ parser. On syntax errors only, the Objective-C++ grammar may be selected when actual Objective-C constructs are observed. Implementation fragments may use an internal implementation envelope only when that parse is complete and real methods/properties exist. Envelope coordinates are deleted before traversal; its empty name emits no declaration or owner. The original source alone determines names, byte offsets, physical lines and chunk coverage.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.identity: objc-/objcpp- source facts use the existing row schema and name byte-offset suffix. Class and instance selector scopes are retained in syntactic qualified terms. Declaration and implementation, including same-line names, retain distinct identities. Selectors preserve every keyword and colon; headers exclude method bodies.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.bounds: Existing 1 MiB source, 200000 syntax-node, parser-progress and 64-level owner/declarator limits remain. Header retries share the same progress and traversal budgets. Source fragments are bounded by the same caps with only a constant parser envelope.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.limits: Syntactic source observation only: no preprocessing, SDK lookup, type checking or call resolution. Upstream grammar does not cover structured bindings or lambda init-captures in Objective-C++; malformed or unsupported syntax remains explicit as syntax-incomplete. Ordinary C++ retains its established grammar.
nativeObjectiveCDevelopment.compatibility: One current reader/writer. Rebuild older indexes explicitly; no compatibility reader or implicit conversion. This source change does not update an installed kit or enrolled project.

parserLimits.overflowPolicy: A source or traversal that reaches a bound does not receive an invented complete tree. The result remains incomplete and bounded; no unbounded parser retry is implied.

spanIdentity.range: start_line and end_line identify the physical raw-line interval selected by the source fact. The interval starts at the first byte of start_line and ends after the end_line newline when present, or at EOF for the final physical line.
spanIdentity.hash: span_hash is FNV-1a-64 over the complete raw bytes of that whole physical-line interval, rendered as fnv1a64:<16 lowercase hexadecimal digits>.
spanIdentity.sharedRanges: Rows with the same path, start_line, and end_line share the same computed span hash.
spanIdentity.identityBoundary: The hash identifies observed source bytes. It is not cryptographic authentication, a semantic identity, a compiler AST identity, behavioral equivalence, or proof that only the named member changed.
spanIdentity.provenance: Syntax ranges are source-fact observations. Range-bearing fact or section records preserve their original status, authority_level, evidence_kind, and verification_level. Current worktree rereads may be labeled observed-worktree only after content and stability checks; published rows retain their snapshot provenance.

relations.store: Structural relations are emitted into the existing docs/kb/generated/links.jsonl store and retain LinkRow fields path, line, kind, text, target, status, and resolved_path.

retool.include: Static Retool Include src observations emit source-include.
retool.payload: Static include(...) observations in supported Retool runtime expressions emit source-payload.
retool.runtimeNameReferences: Lexically observed Retool runtime names, Event pluginId references, and scope bindings emit source-reference candidates. They are structural observations, not calls proven to execute.
retool.scope: Retool bindings and references resolve only within their recorded source scope.

java.binding: Only exact top-level Java declaration bindings are added, keyed by package-qualified type name when a package exists.
java.import: An explicit non-static, non-wildcard qualified Java import references that exact type name. It resolves only when exactly one indexed binding exists in the matching scope and the target path is indexed.

typescript.candidatePolicy: Relative module candidates are bounded and repository-relative. Extensionless targets try .ts, index.ts, .tsx, index.tsx, .js, index.js, .jsx, index.jsx, .mts, index.mts, .cts, index.cts, .mjs, index.mjs, .cjs, and index.cjs. Explicit .js targets also try .ts and .tsx; explicit .mjs and .cjs targets also try .mts and .cts respectively.
typescript.resolution: A candidate resolves only when exactly one valid indexed path matches. No extension preference is used.
typescript.scope: Resolution is bounded to the importing source path's lexical parent and the indexed relative path policy.

failClosed.duplicate: Exact duplicate LinkRows are removed after deterministic sorting; distinct status, target, or resolved_path values remain distinct.
failClosed.ambiguous: More than one binding or module candidate yields status=ambiguous and an empty resolved_path. A non-unique candidate never becomes a guessed edge.
failClosed.unresolved: Recognized relation inputs with missing, unindexed, invalid, escaped, or malformed targets yield status=unresolved and an empty resolved_path. Unsupported syntax imports are skipped and yield no row.
failClosed.graphTraversal: Impact traversal follows source relations with status=resolved and explicit declared document links with status=ok. Unresolved and ambiguous rows remain visible as provenance and omission evidence.

graphReadLimits.producerValidation: The producer rejects publication before writing a valid snapshot when a structural source relation field exceeds 4096 bytes, preventing a later valid publication with an unreadable structural graph.
graphReadLimits.documentLinkBoundary: The 4096-byte bound applies only to structural source relation fields. Preexisting declared document links may carry externally long fields and are not newly classified as corrupt solely by this source-field bound.
graphReadLimits.unsafePolicy: Missing, symlinked, oversized, corrupt, or over-budget structural graph state fails closed; it is not partially accepted as a complete structural graph.

relations.documentLinks: Existing declared document links are traversable when status=ok; their explicit link semantics are retained and are not reclassified as source-import relations.
relations.provenance: Relations are generated evidence from the published snapshot. Declared document links retain declared provenance; structural source-* relations retain source-observed provenance. Neither proves compiler resolution, runtime reachability, or executed behavior.

selectionAndUse.snapshot: Generated-index consumers read one verified published snapshot. Source-scan is not a substitute for this relation graph in the change-aware impact command.
selectionAndUse.worktree: A current worktree reread is separately bounded and reverified. It does not mutate, overlay, or republish the snapshot.
selectionAndUse.scoring: The scoring algorithm and retrieval policy remain unchanged, but new source facts and finer granularity can change observed candidate counts, ordering, selected evidence, and receipts.
selectionAndUse.execution: No source code, tests, build, deployment, business operation, or relation target is executed by extraction or impact selection.
selectionAndUse.publication: No generated index, snapshot, or relation graph is published automatically by these contracts.
selectionAndUse.compaction: No automatic compaction, checkpoint, persistence, or host lifecycle hook is implied.

documentAmbiguities: Exact syntax declarations are limited to the recognized node kinds and safe name fields listed here; this contract does not define every declaration form in any language.

A complete=true syntax observation means the bounded parser traversal reported no error or traversal cap. It is not a compiler validation or a guarantee that the grammar models every language extension.
Java top-level type binding and Java declaration extraction are different scopes: nested methods and constructors may have exact syntax ranges but cannot become top-level type bindings.

TypeScript module resolution is intentionally candidate-based. Unsupported import syntax produces no row; an emitted ambiguous or unresolved row is not evidence that the target does not exist, only that this bounded resolver could not choose one path.
A changed whole-line span hash may include formatting, comments, neighboring declarations, or line-ending changes. It identifies bytes, not behavior or a minimal member edit.
nonGoals: no compiler, type checker, linker, build graph, or semantic call graph
no semantic source diff or behavioral equivalence inference
no runtime reachability, deployment, production, or executed proof
no complete declaration grammar claim for Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, TSX, JSX, C++, C#, or Kotlin
no automatic execution, mutation, publication, index repair, or compaction
no scoring, ranking, query coverage, or retrieval policy change
